summary.text: Sylvia Garcia is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for Texas's 29th District, in office since 2019. A social worker and lawyer by training, she was presiding judge of the Houston municipal court system, Houston city controller, a Harris County commissioner, and a Texas state senator before Congress. She is Vice Ranking Member of the House Financial Services Committee.

paragraphs.text: Garcia was born in San Diego, Texas, in 1950. According to her congressional biography, she grew up in the farming community of Palito Blanco as the eighth of ten children.
She earned a bachelor's degree in social work and political science from Texas Woman's University in 1972 and a J.D. from Thurgood Marshall School of Law at Texas Southern University in 1978.
Early in her career she worked as a social worker and a legal aid lawyer.
Garcia served as director and presiding judge of the Houston Municipal System for five terms under two mayors, according to her congressional biography.

She was elected Houston city controller in 1998 and served two terms, then was elected to the Harris County Commissioners Court, where her biography says she was the first Hispanic and first woman elected in her own right.
She was sworn into the Texas Senate on March 11, 2013, representing District 6, after winning a special runoff election for the seat of the late Sen. Mario Gallegos, and served until 2018.
Garcia was elected to the U.S. House in November 2018 and sworn in on January 3, 2019, becoming the first Latina to represent the 29th District.
She serves as Vice Ranking Member of the House Financial Services Committee, and in January 2020 she was one of seven House managers in the Senate impeachment trial of President Trump.
